title: Count 2,880 five-request binary threshold headers; refute 2 k! (no new κ)
body:
## Summary

For five corank-one requests with pairwise orthogonal rank-one kernels on F_2^6, the exact number of complete passing headers is **2,880**, with density **1/6,999,552**. This answers Open next question 1 of [#4275](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/4275) negatively.

```diff
- Proposed all-k threshold pattern: 2*5! = 240 headers, from two star decompositions
+ Exact five-request certificate: 24*5! = 2,880 headers, including 22 nonstar subsets
```

Claim type: **finite certificate**, with a scoped algebraic bijection and an explicit counterexample to the proposed all-k pattern. The predecessor's proved theorems are unchanged. No new kappa.

Only `research/binary-threshold-five-headers/` is added. The contribution was produced by Nick Petalas. The partial-Gram reduction and threshold argument are credited to the work produced by Nick Petalas in #4275. Cinna Davis supplied the BIT request context; source527, commdata2338 and Jose Manuel retain the normalizer lineage credit.

## Evidence

- **Before:** k = 3,4 suggested two unordered threshold decompositions; k = 5 was explicitly open.
- **After:** all 180 nonzero disjoint-support rectangles, 16,110 pairs and 955,860 triples give exactly 24 unordered five-subsets. The written bijection proves that this is exhaustive for the stated header problem.
- All 2,880 ordered cases are completed to distinct GL_6 headers, inverted and checked against every full conjugated guard chain by literal binary matrix multiplication and no-pivot elimination.
- The displayed nonstar witness can be checked by hand. Five semantic rejection fixtures include a header passing every first guard but failing a later guard. The k = 3,4 positive controls give 12 and 48, agreeing with #4275 and the merged #4345 census. No predecessor verifier is imported or replayed.
- CPython 3.12.15, standard library: direct normal and optimized modes pass in 0.96s and 0.97s; the registered two-command replay passes. Warnings are errors. AST inspection finds a maximum function length of 32 lines.
- Exact committed-byte/source-history checks pass at `c80f445e8c3c22d341d467254b89245fbddb9eb2`. The six-file committed export passes integrity checking and replays with an empty PATH, producing identical scientific output and file hashes.

From the repository root:

```sh
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -W error -B research/binary-threshold-five-headers/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -W error -O -B research/binary-threshold-five-headers/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/binary-threshold-five-headers
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/binary-threshold-five-headers --check-source-history
```

Expected scientific marker: `PASS_BINARY_THRESHOLD_FIVE_HEADERS`. The verifier prints all 24 decompositions and a receipt bound to the six package-file hashes. Full Git history is needed for source-history preflight; the direct verifier is self-contained.

## Limitations

Only k = 5, m = 6 over F_2 and complete equally weighted headers are counted. No all-k formula, odd-field or nonorthogonal extension, physical caller, supplier admission or selected-frontier change is supplied. Selection, emission, dispatch, dirty restoration, stock and precision costs remain unknown. Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed. Selected cold replay, Lean and Docker were not run.

## Related open work

Refreshed this account's open PRs created since the CLAIM at 2026-10-22T09:14:43Z. Besides this PR, the list contains #4597, #4599, #4600 and #4601; their current bodies were read.

- [#4599](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/4599), head `19ca650c67ad2722790dc60c0bfd12989479b06a`, proves the four-request binary full-guard product inequality for the same orthogonal-kernel family. At the overlapping boundary k = 4, m = 5, our saved positive-control receipt gives **48 / 9,999,360 = 1/208,320**, exactly agreeing with its reported **1/208,320**. This comparison uses our enumerated count and its published fraction; no peer verifier was rerun. It supplies no five-request threshold count.
- [#4597](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/4597), head `dfeb8ca729a04aea4aa290438f2ed50a37a9c7cb`, studies a block-Schur commutator for commuting projectors in the related header context. It computes no complete-header probability, so no numerical quantity overlaps this certificate.

#4600 studies depth-four connector short rows, and #4601 studies right-vector costs over local products. Those are different objects and quantities, with no numerical overlap here. No other newly opened account PR studies the five-request threshold count. Merged #4275 supplies the open question; merged #4345 stops at four binary requests in dimension five.

## Open next questions

- Explain the 24 subsets structurally, starting with coordinate-permutation and transposition orbits.
- Find a replacement for the refuted all-k pattern, starting with extension of the displayed five-request partition. No k >= 6 search is included.
- Bind a real producer and fully charge shared-header selection and execution before claiming a physical gain.

## CI notes

In [run 39755026651](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/39755026651), `plan` failed in **Onboarding helper tests**: 331 tests ran, with 4 failures and 11 skips. The package **replay was skipped**, so **hosted CI has not certified this package**. The previously recorded local verification stands unchanged.

The exact four failures in `tests/test_research_current_status.py` are:

- `test_current_ci_section_matches_selected_record`: the CI navigation document's current section lacks `make frontier4359-verify`.
- `test_current_section_matches_selected_record`: the status document has `**0.0023 = 23/10000**`, while the test requires the literal `**0.0023**`.
- `test_history_banner_precedes_historical_sections`: the opening section lacks the required `historical snapshot` banner.
- `test_only_the_first_heading_claims_current_or_selected`: the historical heading still contains `selected`.

All four reproduce on unchanged `origin/main` at `f626db5c3a3d781d8f7695038776c621651f75e1`. An exact export of that commit's test, documents, selected record and referenced metadata ran six tests with exactly these four failures and two passes. Every exported input was also checked byte-for-byte against this worktree. The reproduction command was `/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B -m unittest discover -s tests -p test_research_current_status.py -v`.

The failed logs from two other contributors' runs show the same four tests failing across 331 tests, with four failures and 11 skips: [check-4585, run 39754840618](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/39754840618) and [research/receiver-all-length-floor, run 39746873103](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/39746873103). This is a shared onboarding/documentation failure; no shared docs, tests or certificates were edited. DONE remains pending green CI.

The separately recorded orientation command `scripts/research_baseline.py` reaches `KeyError: 'bit_lower'` in `summarize` against the current selected `research/kappa-rebuild/CLAIM.json`. The helper, selected record and certificate remain unchanged from canonical main `f626db5c3a3d781d8f7695038776c621651f75e1`. That reporter failure is separate from the CI failures above. The full historical helper suite was not run locally.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way. This is an isolated research package.

**Blast Radius:** local. No shared runtime, frozen evidence or selected-result file changes.
